blurb: Large black-masked Turkish flock guardian that protects sheep from wolves
description: The Kangal Shepherd Dog is a large Turkish livestock guardian from Sivas Province with a short fawn to wolf-grey coat and black mask, bred to guard flocks.
answer: The Kangal Shepherd Dog, or Turkish Kangal, is a traditional large livestock guardian from the Kangal district of Sivas Province in central Turkey. Dogs usually stand 72 to 78 cm and bitches 65 to 73 cm. Its coat ranges from pale fawn to wolf grey, always with a black mask, and it has long been kept with flocks to fend off wolves and other predators.

body: The Kangal is a traditional working breed of Central Anatolia that shepherds have used for centuries against wolves and other predators. Its original Turkish name was Karabash, meaning 'blackhead', after the black muzzle; the name Kangal came into use after discussions at the UK Kennel Club in the 1970s. The source describes the breed as originating in Central Asia and arriving with Turkic tribes.

The FCI definitively accepted the breed in 1989, and the UK Kennel Club recognized the Turkish Kangal Dog in 2013. Dogs exported from Turkey since the late 1960s also formed the basis of the American Anatolian Shepherd Dog, a name unknown in Turkey.

The Kangal is a large, powerful dog. Standard heights are 72 to 78 cm for dogs and 65 to 73 cm for bitches, with a 2 cm tolerance, and weights usually run 48 to 60 kg for dogs and 40 to 50 kg for bitches. The moderately short double coat has a dense undercoat and a waterproof outer layer, in colors from pale fawn to wolf grey, always with a black mask.

The Wikipedia source gives little detail on temperament beyond the breed's role as a flock guardian kept with sheep to deter predators. Livestock guardian breeds are generally described by breed clubs as watchful and protective, but individual character varies.

Sources give little specific detail on care or exercise. The Kangal is a working guardian, and since 1994 the Cheetah Conservation Fund has placed around 300 dogs with farmers in Namibia, later extending the program to Kenya, where they protect livestock and reduce the killing of cheetahs.
The Wikipedia source does not describe specific health conditions or lifespan for the breed. Breed clubs generally recommend health screening of breeding stock and regular veterinary check-ups.

faq.q: How big does a Kangal get?
faq.a: Dogs usually stand 72 to 78 cm and weigh 48 to 60 kg, and bitches stand 65 to 73 cm and weigh 40 to 50 kg. It is a large breed.

faq.q: Is the Kangal the same as the Anatolian Shepherd?
faq.a: Not exactly. The Anatolian Shepherd is an American-developed type descended from Turkish guardian dogs, mainly Kangals, and Turkish authorities do not recognize it as a purebred Turkish breed.

faq.q: What is the Kangal used for?
faq.a: It is a traditional flock guardian that protects sheep from wolves and other predators. In Namibia and Kenya, Kangals protect livestock from cheetahs as part of a conservation program.

faq.q: Is the Kangal recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI definitively accepted the breed in 1989, and its most recent standard was published in 2018.
